name: ChuckleFox Comedy Club
description:
Welcome to the ChuckleFox Comedy Club, where laughter reigns supreme, and seriousness takes a backseat! We're not your average comedy joint; we're the place where funny business meets funny bones. Get ready for gut-busting nights, hilarious stand-up, and a side order of snorts and giggles.

Join us for laughs, libations, and a seriously good time – because we're here to prove that comedy isn't just an art, it's a way of life! :D

We are Powai's Premiere Comedy Club, located inside a Co-working space at the Boomerang Building.

featured_reviews.name: Kausthub Sekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Been here several times for live tapings of That Filmy Gameshow. It's located in The Millennial Pod inside The Boomerang Building in Powai/Chandivali. It's accessible via cab, auto and metro with the Saki Naka metro station being the closest though the last mile connectivity leaves a lot to be desired. The host and show runner Antariksh Takkar who is the curator of the shows here including his own award winning podcast That Filmy Gameshow features a ton of the best comic lineups that the city has to offer. They also occasionally run trial shows, concept shows and some lineup shows once in a while.
Here are some glimpses from the latest live taping which had Ashish Shakya of AIB fame and Aadar Malik from the TISS squad.  It's a very cool room and definitely worth a visit with your friends and loved ones especially if you're a Bollywood fan and would like to be part of the live audience for a podcast gameshow recording some time.

featured_reviews.name: Shahid Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text: The Khar Comedy Club, this is the 4th KCC newly opened, easy to travel , to enter you need to enter from main entrance, the building is currently under construction so be carefull, the space is small but that's what make such Comedy shows briliant, around 80-100 people capacity, The vibe is good, chairs are kind of comfortable, went here for Biswas show 'Trying new jox', Enjoyed alot, The food stalls are outside of premises juices, chat and sandwich option available

featured_reviews.name: MANALI GHOSAL
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve been following Khar Comedy Club since its very first days — when shows were happening in a tiny room inside a rented flat for just a few hours. Watching them grow from that humble, makeshift setup to now having their own beautifully designed 100-seater club has been nothing short of inspiring. The interiors are modern, classy, and built with performers and audience comfort in mind. Sound, lights, seating  everything feels professionally set and thoughtfully done.

The team is genuinely lovely, welcoming, and extremely passionate about comedy. They consistently bring the best comedians in the circuit, and still manage to keep ticket prices affordable and audience-friendly, which says a lot about their intent. Every show feels curated, cozy, and full of laughs  exactly what a comedy space should be.
So proud to see how far they’ve come.
If you’re looking for a night of great comedy with an even greater vibe — Khar Comedy Club is your spot!

I went with a friend to watch Manik Mahna’s show, and honestly, Manik was brilliant!

However, the venue left a lot to be desired. After booking the tickets, I checked the reviews and saw that it's a small space and AC doesn't work properly, which came out true and it got quite uncomfortable mid-show. The seating was extremely cramped; there was barely any space between two seats, so you’re practically touching shoulders with strangers on both sides the whole time.

Still, for Manik’s performance, it was worth it. Just wish the venue matched the quality of the comedian.

featured_reviews.name: Eshant Arya
featured_reviews.review_text: Good place for comedy gigs. The place is well located. The ambiance is clean and tidy. Staff were friendly, helpful & they Usher you to your seat. Mocktails and chatarPatar food is also served. The washroom was clean.

featured_reviews.name: Vivek M
featured_reviews.review_text: It was my first time watching a comedy show, and I went to see Devesh Dixit. I arrived 40 minutes early and got entry at 8 PM for the 8 PM show. The place is in the basement and has a nice ambiance. It felt a little congested for seating, but overall it was a good first experience. Nice place to enjoy stand-up comedy.

featured_reviews.name: Aditya Swami
featured_reviews.review_text:
So I had visited on April 18th 2026 and the artists on the poster for the day were Mohammad Hussein, Shamik Chakraborty and Fatima Ayesha.

However only Fatima Ayesha from the main line-up performed and while rest of the line-up of 6-7 odd artists were also quite funny(some were, some not so much), the main problem was deception.

When we asked them about this they pointed to a small disclaimer which stated "Line-up not guaranteed but laughter is".

It was sets of 11-12 min per artist. So overall I don't feel that my money was lost because the line-up was mosty funny however not something for which I would have travelled from afar.

Also it's hard to find but it's just before starbucks.

featured_reviews.name: Akshaya Sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
Great Stand-up Act, But Venue Needs Improvement

Visited The J Spot, Juhu for Manik Mahna’s stand-up show — my first ever live stand-up experience, and it was a good one! Sharon Verma opened the show with a solid set, but Manik Mahna absolutely killed it. His delivery, timing, and presence were top-notch — thoroughly enjoyed his performance.

However, the venue itself left a bit to be desired. There was no staff at the entrance when we arrived, and we had to wait around 15 minutes before someone showed up. The space is quite small and cramped, with very little legroom, which made sitting for a long time a bit uncomfortable.

Overall, a great show but the management and seating experience could definitely be better.

featured_reviews.name: Aishi Ray Chaudhury
featured_reviews.review_text: I came to the show expecting a fun, light-hearted evening, but it turned out to be quite disappointing. From the start, the host felt unprepared and disconnected, and things only got worse when Mayur made a completely distasteful comment that wasn’t even a joke,  just offensive for the sake of it. What really crossed the line, though, were the remarks directed at my friend. When she simply said she doesn’t drink because she doesn’t like it, a cheap comment was thrown in about her being “underage.” Later, an unnecessary and awkward joke was made about her and her boyfriend just because she shared what made her participate in that particular event.
